subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is source-level trajectory exclusion enough to close this issue, or should maintainers require live current-main proof of the reported Windows fresh-session provider-billing path first?
rationale: The code now has several plausible guardrails, but the reported impact is expensive and cross-provider, and this read-only review did not prove the exact runtime path that drove the billing report.

options.title: Require live proof before closing
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or trusted proof lane verifies the fresh-session path with large trajectory sidecars and provider-visible context/token evidence.

options.title: Close from source guardrails
options.body: Treat the current artifact, TUI, memory, and reseed filters as sufficient and close without the exact runtime proof.

options.title: Patch another guardrail first
options.body: Ask for an additional defense around model-context assembly before attempting live closeout proof.

recommendation.title: Require live proof before closing
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or trusted proof lane verifies the fresh-session path with large trajectory sidecars and provider-visible context/token evidence.
